text: When Mother Yashoda tried to tie little Krishna to the mortar, the rope fell short by two fingers.
She added another rope.
Yet, it was still two fingers short.
No matter how much rope she added, the same thing happened.
Finally, when Mother Yashoda was exhausted from her efforts, Krishna himself agreed to be tied.
The Vaishnava tradition gives a beautiful meaning to that two-finger gap:
One finger — our sincere effort.
The other finger — God's grace.
Mother Yashoda made her effort.
Krishna bestowed His grace.
Only then did the rope suffice.
But there's an even more beautiful aspect to this.
Even though the entire universe resides within Him,
Krishna allowed Himself to be bound by a mother's love.
That's why He has the beautiful name “Damodara.”
Dama — rope
Udara — belly
Meaning, “He who has a rope tied around His belly” — Damodara.
But this name reminds us not just of that rope,
But of that infinite Lord,
And that beautiful moment when He was bound by love.
🙏 Om Damodaraya Namah
